summary.text: Tyler Tordsen is a Republican candidate for the South Dakota House of Representatives, District 14, in the November 3, 2026 general election, after advancing from the June 2 Republican primary.
He previously represented District 14 in the House from 2023 to 2025 and worked as a political aide to U.S. Senator Mike Rounds.

paragraphs.text: Tyler Tordsen was born in Sioux Falls, South Dakota, and earned a bachelor's degree from the University of South Dakota in 2015.

In a 2022 Ballotpedia survey, he said he grew up in Rapid City, is an enrolled member of the Sisseton-Wahpeton Sioux Tribe, and studied political science and economics at the University of South Dakota, where he served as student body president.
His career experience includes working as southeast regional director and state director of tribal affairs for U.S. Senator Mike Rounds.
Tordsen won election to the House in November 2022 and assumed office on January 10, 2023, serving on the House Education and House Judiciary committees in the 2023-2024 session.
He lost in the Republican primary for the seat on June 4, 2024, and left office on January 14, 2025.

In the 2022 survey, he listed his campaign messages as limited government and individual liberty, strong communities and healthy families, and a vibrant economy, and named education, business and healthcare as policy interests.
